candidates.change_summary: Change blockAssertion from false to true so the returned AssertionPolicy has blockAssertion = true.
Change arbitrateViaEscalationManager from false to true so the returned AssertionPolicy has arbitrateViaEscalationManager = true.
Change discardOracle from false to true so the returned AssertionPolicy has discardOracle = true.
Change validateDisputers from false to true so the returned AssertionPolicy has validateDisputers = true.
Swap two fields: set blockAssertion = false, arbitrateViaEscalationManager = false, discardOracle = true, validateDisputers = true to return a different combination.
Change return value from unconditionally true to false when disputeCaller equals address(0), otherwise keep true.
Invert the original boolean to always return false instead of true.
Make the function return true only when disputeCaller equals the asserter embedded in the assertion (if available via optimisticAsserter), otherwise false; otherwise fall back to false on errors.
Return a constant non-zero int256 value (1) instead of having an empty body, changing observable return.
Return a constant negative int256 value (-1) instead of empty body, changing observable return.
Return the uint256-converted time parameter as int256, changing output to depend on input time.
Return int256 based on first byte of ancillaryData (0 if empty), making return depend on ancillaryData.
Return hash-based pseudo-random int256 derived from identifier, causing different observable return tied to identifier.
Remove the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier so requestPrice can be called by any caller, changing whether PriceRequestAdded is emitted after calls by non-optimisticAsserter addresses.
Invert emission so the call stores a zeroed identifier when emitting, altering the observable event payload after requestPrice.

Tighten the access check to require sender be address(0), effectively making onlyOptimisticAsserter always revert for normal callers and preventing the event from being emitted; this changes observable behavior of requestPrice.

Make assertionResolvedCallback set a public state-affecting variable by emitting an event instead of being empty, changing observable effects after the call (adds an event emission that external observers can detect).
Change onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier to require the caller is NOT the optimistic asserter (invert check), altering which callers can enter assertionResolvedCallback and thus observable behavior.
Replace empty body with emitting an event to record the assertionId when assertionDisputedCallback is called (changes observable state via event logs).
candidates.mutated_unit_code: function assertionDisputedCallback(bytes32 assertionId) public virtual onlyOptimisticAsserter { emit PriceRequestAdded(assertionId, block.timestamp, abi.encodePacked("disputed")); }

candidates.change_summary: Modify onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier to invert the require so that only non-optimisticAsserter callers can call guarded functions, changing whether assertionDisputedCallback can be called successfully.
candidates.mutated_unit_code: modifier onlyOptimisticAsserter() { require(msg.sender != address(optimisticAsserter), "Not the optimistic asserter"); _; }
